content: Naive round-to-N-decimal-places quantization breaks on IEEE-754 special values: signed zero (-0.0 vs 0.0 compare unequal at the bit level though == treats them equal), denormals/subnormals (flushing to zero is often the correct behavior but changes bit patterns unpredictably depending on FTZ/DAZ mode differences per GPU vendor), and NaN (rounding/truncating a NaN's mantissa bits can flip it to Infinity if the truncation zeros the mantissa; x86 CPUs also canonicalize/rewrite NaN bit patterns to a fixed 0x7FC00000-style pattern on some ops while GPUs preserve payload bits differently, so raw-bytes hashing of NaN payloads diverges across CPU vs GPU even when the numeric 'meaning' -- NaN -- is identical).
